verses.1: I entered my garden, my sister, my bride. I gathered my myrrh with my spices, I ate my honeycomb with my honey, I drank my wine with my milk. Eat, companions, drink, and be drunk, my beloveds.
verses.2: I was asleep, yet my heart was awake. The voice of my beloved was knocking: "Open to me, my sister, my beloved, my dove, my perfect one. My head is drenched with dew, my locks with the drops of night."
verses.3: I undressed my robe—how can I put it on again? I washed my feet—how can I soil them?
verses.4: My beloved thrust his hand through the opening, and my entrails stirred for him.
verses.5: I rose to open for my beloved. My hands dripped with myrrh, my fingers with flowing myrrh, upon the handles of the lock.
verses.6: I opened to my beloved, but my beloved had vanished. My soul went out with his word. I sought him, but did not find him. I called him, but he did not answer me.
verses.7: The watchmen found me, circling the city. They beat me, wounded me; they stripped my veil from me, the guards at the walls.
verses.8: I swear to you, daughters of Jerusalem, if you find my beloved, what will you tell him? That I am faint with love.
verses.9: What is your beloved different from another beloved, O fairest among women? What is your beloved different from another beloved, that you have sworn us so?
verses.10: My beloved is fair and ruddy, distinguished among ten thousand.
verses.11: His head is gold and fine gold, his locks are black like a raven.
verses.12: His eyes are doves, flowing beside streams of water, washed in milk, resting on fullness.
verses.13: His cheeks are like beds of spices, mounds of sweet herbs. His lips are lilies, dripping flowing myrrh.
verses.14: His hands are rods of gold, inlaid with topaz. His belly is a block of ivory, set upon a pedestal of sapphire.
verses.15: His legs are pillars of marble, set upon bases of gold. His appearance is like Lebanon, chosen like cedars.
verses.16: His mouth is sweetness, all of him is desirable. This is my beloved, this is my companion, daughters of Jerusalem.

notes:
Notes
- v. 2: "my locks with the drops of night" reflects the poetic imagery of dewfall during the night.
- v. 8: "O fairest among women" is a paraphrase of "the beautiful among women" to maintain the poetic tone.
- v. 11: "fine gold" is used for פז, which can mean fine gold or gold dust, depending on context.
- v. 14: "topaz" is used for תַּרְשִׁישׁ, although this term is often debated (it could refer to a type of shell or a gemstone).
- v. 15: "chosen like cedars" reflects the elevated status often associated with cedars in Hebrew poetic imagery.
